Education system 2

Discuss the Thai education system and its problems, in Thai. This topic tackles the debates — fierce แข่งขัน (competition) for top universities, the ever-changing ทีแคส (TCAS) admissions, แป๊ะเจี๊ยะ (tea money) for sought-after places, and ท่องจำ (rote learning) that leaves students weak at critical thinking. It covers stress and ความยากจน (poverty), the city-provincial quality gap, valuing the ใบปริญญา (degree certificate) over real ability, and why some give up and study เมืองนอก (overseas). All 26 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations, and word-by-word notes, so it all lands by ear.

TCAS (the Thai University Central Admission System) is the centralised university-entrance process: applicants choose faculties (คณะ) and compete on exam scores. Frequent rule changes are a standing source of complaint.

Before state schooling spread, temples were the main route to literacy, especially in the rural northeast (อีสาน). Boys lived at the local wat as เด็กวัด, serving the monks who taught them in return; girls were largely excluded — one root of older-generation literacy gaps.
